recipes.name: The Old Boy's Strawberry Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 recipe pastry for a 9 inch single crust pie

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Place a drip pan on the lowest oven rack to catch pie juices.
Press pie crust into a 9-inch pie dish. Combine 3/4 cup sugar, 3/4 cup flour, 6 tablespoons butter, and nutmeg in a medium bowl until fluffy; set topping aside.

Add strawberries to a large bowl. Combine remaining 1/2 cup sugar, remaining 1/2 cup flour, and cornstarch together in a separate bowl; add to strawberries, stirring gently until coated, being careful not to crush berries.

Pour strawberries into prepared pie crust, mounding them in the middle as berries will sink as they bake. Cover strawberries with topping; top with about 15 pea-sized pieces of butter. Wrap edges of pie crust with foil to prevent burning.

Bake in the preheated oven for 20 minutes, then reduce heat to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) and bake 40 minutes more. With 10 minutes left of baking, sprinkle a little extra sugar over crumb topping, then finish baking.

raw_recipe.headline: The Old Boy's Strawberry Pie
raw_recipe.description: This strawberry crumb pie with fresh strawberries, nutmeg, and a purchased pie crust, unite into an easy to make summertime pie like you've never tasted.

review.reviewBody: By utilizing the suggestions of previous reviewers and adding a couple of my own, this pie turned out beautifully. I'll definitely be making this pie again and again. Here's what I recommend. 1) Taste your strawberries first to determine how sweet they are. This will help you decide how much sugar to use. 2) As suggested by a previous reviewer, discard the excess sugar, flour and cornstarch mixture to prevent your pie from becoming goopy and soupy. 3) Make a brown sugar oatmeal crumble topping for your pie by combining one stick of butter, 1 cup brown sugar, 3/4 cup oatmeal, 3/4 cup flour, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon and a pinch of salt. The topping will be beautiful and brown.

A pie that doesn't turn out is worthy of *no* stars. Not even if the topping was good, which this was. I should have expected it. A half cup of flour and a tablespoon of cornstarch is waaaaay too much thickener for four cups of ANY kind of fruit and I should have followed my gut and trusted my 50 years of baking experience. I even used five cups of berries and it still was a pasty, raw floury, unappetizing goo. (This literally WAS inedible - I'm not exaggerating merely to stress a point) It was a beautiful pie, I'll give it that, because the crust was great (Harden Your Arteries Pie Crust) and the topping was beautiful and delicious. But the disaster is obvious immediately upon cutting into it. Had this recipe called for half the amount of thickener I might have ended up with a decent pie, but the recipe is what it is and, if prepared as is with the error in the ingredients, is simply awful and a failure. (For those of you who are interested, I have posted a personal photo of the cut slice which is worth a thousand words)

Awesome! For the life of me I don’t understand why people change a recipe before they even try it first. There’s nothing wrong with this recipe, it’s very good. I’m 83 years YOUNG and an I make an excellent pie with a from-scratch crust. I live in Wisconsin and most of the time our strawberries aren’t too sweet but they are often huge! Common sense tells you to at least half or quarter them which I did. To make the crumb or strudel topping for a pie, you never use brown sugar and oatmeal! You’re making a PIE not a crisp or a crumble. The pie is great just as it is. Oh, by the way, since putting foil on the edge of the crust, which I find difficult working on an already hot pie, get aluminum rings to put on when the edge is getting too brown. They’re inexpensive, come in various sizes to fit all size pie plates, and work like a charm. Happy baking everyone!

I make this pie all the time. Like others said- melt the butter in the topping. I also switch out about 1/4 c of the white sugar in the topping for brown sugar. I have made this pie with blueberries and cherries added to the strawberries and I like it even more. My oven tends to need a little more time for this pie.

I had been looking at this recipe for some time wondering if it would work with frozen strawberries from last summer's abundant crop and finally gave it a whirl. I also decided to make the original with no exceptions other than the frozen berries. It was a huge success! Rather than discard the leftover sugar-flour coating I added it to the crumb topping mixture and then gave everything a whirl in the food processor which made the topping very fine. I then spread on top allowing it to filter down into the berries. After the hour baking time it did not look done enough in the center, most likely due to the frozen berries, so I ended up adding an additional 15-20 minutes baking time. The pie was still warm when sliced and there was absolutely no runny, gooey mess--just an absolutely delicious pie that would go well with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. It was an appropriate ending to Pi (e) Day!

We absolutely love this recipe, I’ve made it several times now. And friends always request it when I offer to bring a dessert. The recipe doesn’t mention melting the butter before adding to the flour and sugar to make the crumb topping. That’s the only way to get the crumb topping “fluffy”. Other than that I’ve followed exactly.

I had HUGE sweet strawberries so I roughly cut them into smaller chunks (app 6 cups). I made half of the cornstarch mixture and had none wasted. I used brown sugar in the topping. Overall sweetness of finished pie was perfect! Let cool down on counter and chill for several hours-before cutting. DO use parchment underneath pie plate on top of low sided pan- it WILL run over!
Delicious. I reduced sugar in the filling to 2/3 cup so it'd be more tart, and added 1 tsp lemon rind. I also reduced sugar by 50% in the crumb topping and turned out great.

Like others, I made a few changes: I used less sugar and less flour. For the crumb topping I used 1/2 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup flour, 1/4 cup oats, and 6 Tbsps. butter. For the strawberries I used only 1/2 cup granulated sugar and 2 Tbsps. corn starch (no additional flour). I also increased the amount of strawberries to 6 cups. I always use 6 cups of fruit for my fruit pies. The consistency was spot on, and the flavor was great! Strawberries are a sweet fruit, and I don't really think that more than one cup of sugar (1/2 C for topping and 1/2 C for filling) is necessary. It was delightful!

Not bad. My man really enjoyed it. I used 6 cups of strawberries. I didn't have any cornstarch so didn't add it. I've never used cornstarch in my pie before. Before adding crumble topping I placed pads of butter on top of the strawberry filling. I then put on topping and placed pads of butter on top of that too. The crumble came out nice and crunchy.

If I had made it based on the original recipe, I probably would have been disappointed but I have learned over the years to take other reviewers notes into consideration. I did as other said and threw away the extra flour/sugar mix after I mixed the strawberries in it. I also made the crumble with brown sugar instead of white. It did make way too much so next time I will cut that in half. Finally in the last step of cooking it recommends sprinkling the top with sugar. I skipped that and didn’t miss it. So happy with the results of this. It’s best described as a hybrid pie/crumble.
We love this pie. Hard to find a baked strawberry pie that’s good. Follow the recipe closely and it will be yummy. Love the topping!

First time ever to comment on a recipe. But I have to- because I have to clarify the misstep that is leading to the small handful of negative reviews. This is my husband's favorite pie recipe and I love it for its' simplicity. I use a frozen pie crust, I quarter the berries (sometimes add blueberries) and add a bit of lemon zest. Otherwise I follow the recipe fairly precisely. The misstep- the filling! The sugar/flour/ cornstarch is strictly to coat the berries! Do NOT dump the whole bowl into your crust!!!! Coat the berries well with that mixture and then scoop out gently with your fingers and put into pie crust. Only coated berries go into the pie crust- not loose flour and sugar etc.!!!! You will have leftover flour sugar cornstarch. Don't put it in- it's okay. Hope that helps. Enjoy!

This has been my go-to strawberry pie for quite a few years now. It's awesome. I've modified it by combining blackberries and raspberries or blueberries to equal 4 cups, added apples and rhubarb, but the straight up strawberry as written is my personal favorite. I love all things strawberry and this pie is at the top of my list every year. It works with frozen berries too, I just let them thaw a but, and increase the flour and cornstarch to compensate for the liquid increase frozen in the berries. I loooove this recipe!! You will not regret trying it.
This was fabulous! I don’t know why strawberry pies aren’t more popular! I made it as is but you do need to melt the butter (it doesn’t say to do in case you are wondering!).

I used the suggested oatmeal topping with a bit less sugar. I used whole wheat flour instead of white. I should have quartered the strawberries instead of halving them. The resulting pie came out well but the strawberries did not shrink in the middle after heaping them. It cooked well and resembled a hill. Strawberries did not lose their integrity after cooking--firm and juicy. The sauce was not too sweet, not too tart. I will use this recipe again.

As good as it claims, easy (except for hulling all those berries), and unique. You need to halve or quarter those big, nuclear strawbs from the supermarket; the sugar won’t reach the interior of those and they’ll taste sour compared to the pie’s heavenly pink sauce.
